predecessors.name: Nguyễn lords
predecessors.text: Qui Nhơn (Bình Định) from 1773, the south-central coast from 1775 and Gia Định from 1776-1777

predecessors.name: Trịnh lords
predecessors.text: the northern outline, Đàng Ngoài, taken in 1786-1788

successors.name: Nguyễn dynasty (Đại Nam)
successors.text: the northern rump (Thăng Long/Bắc Thành and the north) and the rest of the Tây Sơn lands, taken by Nguyễn Ánh between 1799 and 1802

rulers.name: Nguyễn Nhạc (Thái Đức)
rulers.title: rebel leader; Tây Sơn vương from 1776; emperor Thái Đức 1778-1788

ledger.x: 1771: the three Nguyễn brothers of Tây Sơn village rise against the Nguyễn lord Phúc Thuần.
1773: the Tây Sơn take the port of Qui Nhơn.
1775: the Tây Sơn take Quảng Nam and the coast to the south of it.
1776: Nguyễn Nhạc titles himself Tây Sơn vương and makes Đồ Bàn (the citadel, in Bình Định by my reading) his capital ('used Đồ Bàn Citadel as his capital'; infobox 'Đồ Bàn (1776-1788)').
1776: the Tây Sơn reach the last Nguyễn stronghold.
1777: the fighting for Gia Định ends.
1777: Gia Định and the delta pass to the Tây Sơn.
1778: Nguyễn Ánh returns from hiding and retakes Saigon.
1778: Nguyễn Nhạc proclaims himself emperor (Thái Đức).
1782: the Tây Sơn retake Gia Định.
1783: Gia Định changes hands.
1784: the Siamese fleet comes to help Nguyễn Ánh.
1785: Ánh, 'forced to become a refugee in Siam in 1785', ends the contest for Gia Định; he returns and retakes Saigon on 7 September 1788.
20 January 1785: the Siamese fleet is destroyed at Rạch Gầm-Xoài Mút.
1786: the Tây Sơn take Phú Xuân.
1786: Huệ marches on the north.

1787: the Trịnh lords end (page silent on the year here: the trinh-lords dossier cites 'Trịnh Bồng was defeated by Chỉnh in fall 1787, ending Trịnh rule' from the Trịnh lords page; Quang Trung page only: 'Northern Vietnam fell into chaos in 1786').
1788: the capital moves from Đồ Bàn to Phú Xuân (infobox: Phú Xuân 1788-1801).
1788: the Tây Sơn hold the north, the land of the Trịnh lords (Đàng Ngoài).
7 September 1788: Nguyễn Ánh retakes Saigon for good.
November 1788: the Qing invade the north.
22 December 1788: Nguyễn Huệ proclaims himself Emperor Quang Trung on Bân Hill at Phú Xuân.
January-February 1789: Quang Trung beats the Qing at Ngọc Hồi-Đống Đa.
1791: the northern uplands join the Tây Sơn shape (counterpart nobody: no state is recorded for them; Cliopatria's Lê row ended in 1571).
16 September 1792: Quang Trung dies; his ten-year-old son Cảnh Thịnh is enthroned, with his uncle Bùi Đắc Tuyên in real power (Quang Trung page, Dynasty page).
1793: the Nguyễn attack Quy Nhơn.
1794: Khánh Hòa and part of the Central Highlands pass to Nguyễn Ánh.
1796: Phú Yên passes to Nguyễn Ánh.
1799: Nguyễn Ánh takes the citadel of Quy Nhơn.
1800: the Tây Sơn hold Quy Nhơn again.
1801: Quy Nhơn and the south fall to Nguyễn Ánh.
1801: the Tây Sơn court withdraws from Phú Xuân to Thăng Long, called Bắc Thành (infobox: Bắc Thành 1801-1802).
3 May 1801: Nguyễn Ánh takes Phú Xuân.
1802: the long war with Nguyễn Ánh ends in his victory.

20 July 1802: Nguyễn Ánh captures Hanoi and the Tây Sơn end; Quang Toản is captured and executed and the Nguyễn dynasty rules the whole country (Dynasty page: 'Nguyễn Ánh captured Đông Kinh on 18 June 1802'; Gia Long page: 22 July). Ánh had been crowned at Huế on 1 June 1802 as Gia Long (Nguyễn dynasty page).

wars.name: Trịnh-Nguyễn War (1774-1775 phase)
wars.outcome: The Trịnh took Huế in February 1775 and left 'the destruction of the Nguyễn to the southern rebels' after a treaty with Nhạc; Thuận Hóa became a Trịnh viceroyalty.

wars.name: Tây Sơn conquest of the Nguyễn lords
wars.outcome: The Tây Sơn took Qui Nhơn (1773), the south-central coast (1775) and Gia Định (1776-1777); the Nguyễn lords were destroyed in 1777, Nguyễn Ánh alone escaping.

wars.name: Nguyễn Ánh's war for Gia Định (Tây Sơn-Siamese war)
wars.outcome: Ánh retook Gia Định in 1778 and lost it in 1782-1783; Siam attacked in 1780 and 1784-1785 and lost its fleet at Rạch Gầm-Xoài Mút on 20 January 1785; Ánh fled to Siam and retook Saigon on 7 September 1788.

wars.name: Battle of Rạch Gầm-Xoài Mút
wars.outcome: Huệ destroyed the Siamese fleet on 20 January 1785; the Tây Sơn kept Gia Định until 1788.

wars.name: Qing invasion of Đại Việt (Sino-Vietnamese war of 1788-1789)
wars.outcome: The Qing army entered Thăng Long in November-December 1788 and was routed at Ngọc Hồi-Đống Đa in late January-February 1789; the Lê dynasty ended on 3 February 1789 and the Qianlong Emperor recognised Huệ as King of Annam.

wars.name: Tây Sơn invasion of Vientiane
wars.outcome: 'In 1791, Vientiane was invaded by the Vietnamese Tây Sơn dynasty to root out Lê dynasty loyalists'; Nanthasen later reached an accommodation with the Tây Sơn.

wars.name: Nguyễn Ánh's conquest of the Tây Sơn (1789-1802)
wars.outcome: Ánh took Quy Nhơn in 1799 and 1801, Phú Xuân on 3 May 1801 and Hanoi on 20 July 1802, ending the Tây Sơn.

certainty.note: All frontiers are approximate: the Hải Vân Pass and the Gianh River are the only lines the pages name; the Central Highlands are never mentioned; the Tonkin uplands are drawn from Cliopatria.
